name: Sri Lanka
headline: Sri Lanka: +5.0% growth in 2025, −0.5% inflation, debt 97% of GDP
sections: Sri Lanka is a $109 billion economy (2025), the world's 73rd-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +5.0% in 2025, faster than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $17K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 17.1% of GDP (2025).
Consumer prices rose −0.5% in 2025, in deflation, down from 45.2% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 3.9% (2025), below the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 18.6% (2025).
Gross government debt is 97% of GDP (2025), a elevated level. The general government balance is −2.3% of GDP (2025).
The current account balance is +1.6% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 42% of GDP (2025), a relatively closed economy. Net FDI inflows were 1.0% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 82% of GDP by 2031, on a declining path from today's level. Life expectancy is 77.7 years (2024). Population: 21.8 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
